entries.title: Matthew 7:1
segments:
Judge not., etc.  Those who would escape criticism must not be faultfinders.
 

 
Mete. That is, measure.

entries.title: Matthew 7:3
segments:
Mote Literally, a small particle of dust, cloth, or a splinter or small twig.
 

 
Beam A stick of large timber.  The mote and the beam were often figuratively used in Jewish controversy.  The mote stood for a small fault, the beam for a serious sin.  Jesus here means by it want of charity in thought and speech.

entries.title: Matthew 7:6
segments:
That which is holy Literally, the meat offerings in the Jewish sacrifices.  Here are meant the truths of religion.
 

 
Dogs...swine While reproving faultfinding, our Lord commands that we should not err in the opposite direction.  We are not to praise men indiscriminately, or without discretion to offer them the pearls of religious truth, for among those thus praised and favored will be the brutal, the blasphemous and the cruel.

entries.title: Matthew 7:7
segments: Ask, seek, knock A series of increasingly patient and aggressive attempts to realize the relation of the soul to God, to gain his favor and direction.  We are never to despair, for the victory is promised to those who persevere.

entries.title: Matthew 7:12
segments: All things therefore. The Golden Rule is the one great light needed to be thrown upon the dark problems of society.  Other great religious teachers announce it in negative form or limit its application.  Jesus alone makes it positive, constructive and universal.  He takes it beyond the narrow range of relatives, friends, neighbors, or of the tribe and nation.  He makes it the foundation of the personal life in society.  'Do not do unto others that which you would not have them do unto you,' is only good advice, a maxim of precaution, a preparation for doing good.  Jesus goes far beyond this.  He speaks to individual men and women and at once makes them active contributors to the justice, kindness and happiness of the world.

entries.title: Matthew 7:13
segments: Narrow gate.. Eastern cities were usually surrounded by walls.  The gates in the walls were generally narrow and difficult to pass through.  Hence the saying about the broad and the narrow way, which was in common use among the Jews.  Few are willing to practice self-denial, to accept the rule of the Spirit which leads to life, while the way of the world is broad and easy, and agrees with the natural inclinations.  It leads to destruction.

entries.title: Matthew 7:15
segments: Beware of false prophets. Those who knew the way of life, but were not sincere in their motives and intentions.  They were professed believers in Christ  (

entries.title: Matthew 7:16
segments: Fruits. Their acts; their moral conduct

entries.title: Matthew 7:19
segments: Is hewn down, etc.  This is still a custom in the East.

entries.title: Matthew 7:21
segments:
Lord. Taken in connection with the clause following, the title which Jesus here applies to himself can only mean that he is Lord of the universe, the ruler of the kingdom of heaven of which he speaks.
 

 
He that doeth. Again in this discourse he brings all professions to the test of obedience.

entries.title: Matthew 7:22
segments: That day. Jesus here speaks of a future when his life and teaching shall be in control, when it will be worth while, in fact a protection, to profess belief in him.

entries.title: Matthew 7:23
segments:
I never knew you. This implies the omniscience of Christ, one of its manifestations being the power to know the true spiritual condition of all who come before him.
 

 
Iniquity. Literally, what is contrary to law.

entries.title: Matthew 7:24
segments: A wise man, who built his house upon the rock. The hearing and the doing of Christ's words, taken together, are the highest wisdom, the only sure foundation.  The first step in the doing is the first stone in that foundation, built upon the rock, which is Christ himself.

entries.title: Matthew 7:26
segments: And doeth them not. The emphasis of Jesus upon the uselessness of hearing without doing suggests the great warning of this parable.  Indifference and inaction after hearing are the chief dangers.

entries.title: Matthew 7:29
segments: Not as their scribes.. The great contrast was this: the scribes were accurate copyists and narrow expounders of the Mosaic law and were constantly appealing to its authority; Jesus spoke as the source of authority, with power to revise and amend the law.
